issues.description: Mutating shared TritonLoraConfig.is_registered without a lock is a race waiting to happen
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request mutates lora_config.is_registered after sending weights. The TritonLoraConfig instances live on TritonModelMetadata and are shared across all concurrent requests. Two concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA will both see is_registered=False, both will load and send weights, and worse — if one flips the flag before the other actually sends, subsequent requests may skip weights before the backend has registered them. Async FastAPI handlers make this concrete. Either guard with a per-config asyncio.Lock, send weights every time the engine reports it doesn't know the task_id, or have the backend confirm registration. As written this is non-deterministic correctness, not a style nit.

issues.description: _get_lora_config will NPE when model_name is unknown
issues.detail: self.model_metadata.get(model_name) can return None, and the very next line dereferences model_metadata.lora_configs. The callers in chat()/completion() pass model_name that was already validated upstream in this code path, but writing a helper that crashes the server on a lookup miss instead of raising ClientError is hostile to the next maintainer. Either assert and raise, or use [] indexing so the failure mode is obvious. Don't ship the silent AttributeError.

issues.description: task_id allocation is global across models and not reset on reload
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 and increments across every LoRA in every model in every repo path in a single _parse_lora_configs call, but the function is called per-model in _get_model_metadata. That means every model's LoRAs start from task_id=1, so two different models with LoRAs will hand identical task_ids to the TRT-LLM backend. If the backend's task_id namespace is per-model that's fine, but the code doesn't document that assumption and the TRT-LLM docs treat lora_task_id as a cache key. State the invariant in the code or make the IDs globally unique. Right now it's coincidence-driven.

issues.description: Backend dispatch logic in _get_model_metadata is unreadable
issues.detail: `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend` inverts the obvious reading — you'd expect self.backend to be the override, not the fallback. Combined with the earlier `if self.backend == "vllm" or backend == "vllm"` that was removed, the new caller now silently passes whatever string into _parse_lora_configs and the function does `if backend == "vllm": ... else: # assume TRT-LLM`. An ensemble or python backend will be treated as TRT-LLM and may blow up on missing .npy files. Make the dispatch explicit and reject unknown backends rather than defaulting them into the LoRA-tensor-loading path.

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production code
issues.detail: `print(f"backend: {backend}")` inside the parse loop and `print(traceback.format_exc())` in three FastAPI routers and in _parse_lora_configs are debugging scaffolding. Servers should use the logging module with a proper level, not stdout prints that bypass log routing, log rotation, and structured logging. The traceback dumps also leak internal paths to operators who configured log levels deliberately. Strip these or convert to logger.exception().

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path reused for two different things
issues.detail: In _parse_lora_configs, `lora_config_path` is first set to the path of multi_lora.json, then reassigned inside the loop to the path of model.lora_config.npy. The outer `with open(lora_config_path, "r")` is already past, so it works, but the next maintainer reading this will assume the inner variable refers to the same thing. Rename one of them — `lora_tensor_config_path` for the .npy file is fine.

issues.description: Silent return None on malformed JSON swallows real errors
issues.detail: The except Exception in the multi_lora.json parse block catches ServerError separately and re-raises, but the generic except returns None and the only signal is a printed traceback. A malformed multi_lora.json silently disables LoRA for that model with no error surfaced to the operator. Either propagate, log at error level, or return a structured failure — but don't pretend nothing went wrong.

issues.description: Three-patches: this PR mixes feature, error-handling, and doc changes
issues.detail: This patch does (1) the actual multi-LoRA TRT-LLM feature, (2) traceback-print error handling in three FastAPI routers, and (3) a docs rewrite. The router error-handling change touches every endpoint including embeddings, which has nothing to do with LoRA. Split into three. The router change in particular should be reviewed on its own merits — printing tracebacks to stdout from exception handlers is a logging policy decision that doesn't belong hidden inside a feature PR.

_parse_lora_configs returns List[TritonLoraConfig] but the annotation says `None | List[tuple[str, str]]`. The old annotation from _get_vllm_lora_names was never updated. This is the kind of thing static analysis catches if you run it, and the next person to touch the function will trust the lying annotation.

issues.description: is_registered=False default on Optional[bool] field is dishonest
issues.detail: `is_registered: Optional[bool] = False` declares the field can be None but defaults to False and is only ever read as a truthy bool. Either it's Optional and the consumer handles None, or it's bool and defaults to False. Pick one. Same for path/task_id — these are required when the config refers to a TRT-LLM LoRA and meaningless when vLLM; a sum type or two dataclasses would model this honestly. The current shape lets a vLLM LoRA reach _create_trtllm_generate_request and crash on lora_config.task_id being None inside np.uint64.

issues.description: List comprehension in two validators duplicates work
issues.detail: `lora_name not in [lora_config.name for lora_config in metadata.lora_configs]` builds a list to do an `in` check, in two places. A set comprehension or a helper method on metadata (`metadata.lora_names()`) would be more honest about intent and avoid the duplication. Minor, but it's the same idiom twice and the abstraction is staring you in the face.

issues.description: Test parametrization tests vllm and tensorrtllm under the same expected-error contract
issues.detail: `test_parse_lora_configs` now calls parse_lora_configs twice with different backends but the expect_error contract is shared. If TRT-LLM parsing fails differently from vLLM parsing for the same input, the test won't distinguish. Either split into two parametrize entries or assert backend-specific behavior. Not a blocker but the test got weaker, not stronger, in the rename.

issues.description: sed-based config.pbtxt patching with FIXME comment in test infrastructure
issues.detail: The FIXME-tagged sed lines patching `dims: [ -1, 3 ]` to `dims: [ -1, 4 ]` in tensorrt_llm and tensorrt_llm_bls config.pbtxt is a workaround pinned to a TRT-LLM version. Track it with an issue link, not a bare FIXME. When TRT-LLM updates, this silently breaks or silently succeeds depending on whether the dims string still exists.

review.summary: The feature is real and the test coverage is decent, but the patch ships with at least one concurrency bug (shared is_registered flag mutated without a lock under async FastAPI), a NoneType deref in _get_lora_config, ambiguous backend dispatch that defaults unknown backends into the TRT-LLM tensor-loading path, and global task_id allocation that may or may not collide across models depending on undocumented backend assumptions. On top of that the PR mixes a LoRA feature with print-debugging across three unrelated routers and a docs rewrite — that's three patches, not one. NEEDS-WORK. Split the router error-handling and docs into their own patches, fix the race on is_registered, fix the NPE, document or fix the task_id namespace, kill the debug prints, and fix the lying return-type annotation. Then it lands.
